question: What is the primary function of the lacrimal gland secretion's enzyme, lysozyme?

options.A: Dilating the pupil in dim light
options.C: Destroying bacteria on the eye surface

explanation: Lysozyme is an antimicrobial enzyme present in tears that helps protect the eye by breaking down bacterial cell walls and preventing infection. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which condition directly results from a blockage in the nasolacrimal duct?

options.A: Excessive tearing spilling over the cheek
options.B: Inability to close the eyelid completely
options.D: Double vision caused by muscle weakness

explanation: When the nasolacrimal duct is blocked, tears cannot drain properly into the nasal cavity, leading to overflow known as epiphora. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is the cornea able to remain completely transparent despite lacking blood vessels?

options.A: It is continuously washed by pure sterile water from the sclera
options.B: It receives nutrients by diffusion from aqueous humor and tears
options.C: It contains specialized transparent blood capillaries
options.D: It is composed entirely of dead, keratinized epithelial cells

explanation: The absence of blood vessels preserves clarity, relying instead on surrounding fluids for metabolic exchange. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h2)

question: What structural feature of the choroid directly enhances visual acuity?

options.A: Glands that secrete lubricating mucus onto the retina
options.B: Thick cartilage plates that maintain eyeball shape
options.C: Dark pigmentation that absorbs scattered light rays
options.D: Skeletal muscle fibers that contract during focusing

explanation: The dark melanin pigment within the choroid prevents light reflection inside the eyeball, ensuring crisp and clear image formation on the retina. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h2)

question: Where on the human retina is visual acuity the absolute highest due to a dense concentration of cones?
explanation: The fovea centralis sits at the exact center of the macula lutea and contains exclusively packed cones, yielding the sharpest detail vision. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the structural reason the optic disc is referred to as the physiological blind spot?

options.A: It receives no blood supply and undergoes rapid cell death
options.B: It is covered by a thick layer of pigmented melanin cells
options.C: It is constantly shadowed by the blood vessels of the choroid layer
options.D: It contains only exiting nerve fibers and lacks photoreceptor cells

explanation: Because ganglion cell axons bundle here to form the optic nerve, no rods or cones are present to detect light stimuli. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary fluid found within the posterior segment of the eyeball?
explanation: The transparent, gelatinous vitreous humor fills the large posterior cavity, helping maintain the spherical shape of the eye and supporting the retina. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient is diagnosed with closed-angle glaucoma. What underlying physiological problem has occurred?

options.A: Total collapse of the cornea due to lack of local blood supply
options.B: Overproduction of vitreous humor by the embryonic retina
options.C: Rapid deterioration of photoreceptor cells within the fovea
options.D: Blocked drainage of aqueous humor into the scleral venous sinus

explanation: Glaucoma results from impaired outflow of aqueous humor, causing fluid buildup and dangerous increases in internal eye pressure. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h4)

question: What structural change occurs in the lens when an individual shifts their gaze from a distant mountain to read a nearby textbook?

options.A: It flattens out and decreases total refractive power
options.B: It becomes more convex and increases refractive power
options.C: It moves forward into the anterior chamber of the eye
options.D: It hardens completely and stops refracting light rays

explanation: Accommodation for near vision requires the lens to thicken and round out, which bends divergent light rays more sharply onto the retina. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a correct description of common refractive vision errors?

options.A: Hyperopia occurs when light focuses behind the retina due to a short globe
options.B: Astigmatism results from unequal curvature of the cornea or lens
options.C: Myopia is corrected using a convex lens to converge light rays earlier
options.D: Presbyopia involves age-related loss of lens elasticity and focusing ability

explanation: Myopia is corrected using a concave lens to diverge incoming light rays so they focus further back, directly onto the retina. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h5)

question: What vitamin derivative is an essential structural component of the light-sensitive pigment rhodopsin?
explanation: Retinal, the light-absorbing part of rhodopsin, is synthesized directly from vitamin A, which explains why deficiency leads to night blindness. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h6)

question: What anatomical event occurs at the optic chiasm during the processing of visual information?

options.A: Aqueous humor drains from the anterior cavity into the venous circulation
options.B: All visual signals are completely inverted before reaching the thalamus
options.C: Fibers from the medial half of each retina cross to the opposite side of the brain
options.D: Photoreceptor cells regenerate their exhausted rhodopsin pigment molecules

explanation: The optic chiasm is the site of partial decussation, ensuring that visual information from each visual field is processed in the contralateral hemisphere. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h6)
